newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 27.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
-- ROCHE ACQUIRES DIAGNOSTICS GROUP FOR $11 BILLION

Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche is to pay 11 billion dollars to acquire leading medical diagnostics group Boehringer Mannheim. The acquisition is the largest in Roche's history and will make the company a world leader in the estimated 19 billion dollar per year illness diagnostic equipment market. Roche chairman Fritz Gerber believes that the combination of his group and BM will aid in the disease management and patient care areas which have recently gained in importance due to "continuing efforts to reduce healthcare costs".
-- SELL-OFFS "COULD PRODUCE 15 BILLION STERLING FOR GOVT"

Keith Boyfield has issued a study entitled the European Policy Forum in which he declares that through privatisation, franchising, and the sale of state-owned property, the UK government could raise 15 billion sterling over its five-year term. Boyfield claimed that with the money, Labour could meet its public expenditure goals while eliminating the possibility of tax increases or borrowing. Among the companies he lists as possible asset sales are the Post Office, Channel Four, Manchester Airport and the DSS.
-- BANKS ACT ON OPERATIONAL RISKS

A recent survey carried out by the British Bankers' Association and accountancy firm Coopers & Lybrand has estimated that over two-thirds of banks view operational risks as being equally significant to the traditional banking perils. In light of the study and pressure from regulators, UK banks have increased their efforts to cut down on fraud and computer failure, and 'rogue traders' and the mille nnium bug problem have also been labelled as particularly dangerous problems. The Bank of England has introduced its own risk-based supervision structure and has pressured other banks to follow suit. --
PRUDENTIAL TOP INVESTOR, SAYS CITY ANALYST

An analysis to be released by independent management data provider Citywatch has revealed that the Prudential Corporation is the largest UK-based institutional investor. The Prudential currently has 91 billion sterling under management, three billion sterling more than its closest rival Schroder, and five billion sterling more than Mercury Asset Management. MAM, however, is the largest inv estor at 41 billion sterling, followed by Prudential at 32 billion sterling and Schroeder at 29 billion sterling. The Citywatch report covered 209 institutional investors, with a total of 1.8 trillion sterling in assets.
-- PARTNERSHIP SET TO TAKE ON MOBILE PHONE GIANTS

Hertfordshire-based consultancy the Technology Partnership has emerged as a surprise rival to mobile phone giants such as Nokia, Ericsson and Motorola. The Techology Partnership is currently providing software to Vodaphone for its phone trials and has teamed up with the US' Qualcomm in a project aimed at developing a mobile phone which would operate anywhere in the world. The partnership also esti mates that it controls ten percent of the market for the inner workings of mobile phones and has sold one million units since its GSM chip-set was approved.
-- SIGNET CRITIC BACKS REORGANISATION

The capital reorganization of UK jewellery group Signet has received backing from one of its largest shareholders, the UK Active Value Fund. The AVF believes the moves at Signet will bring out its 'underlying value', and other Signet shareholders such as Everest Capital and Sass Associates are also expected to declare their support. Signet's restructuring plans will include measures to switch its eight classes of convertible shares into ordinary shares in an attempt to create a unified share structure and in return for 165 million sterling in waived dividend arrears from preference holders.
-- 14 MILLION STG IRISH DEAL SET TO DOUBLE ETHICAL'S REVENUES

Cambridge-based biotech company Ethical Holdings has announced that it is to purchase Irish pharmaceuticals group Clonmel Healthcare for an estimated 14 million stg. The deal is expected to double revenues at Ethical and significantly increase the number of employees at the biotech firm which has made plans to list in London at 20 million stg. Ethical chief executive Geffrey Guy played down compar isons between his company and troubled Cellnet, stating Ethical is 'at the low-risk end of drug development' with proven ability to make profits.
-- POWERHOUSE 4.7 MILLION STG FOR NINE MONTHS

The largest independent electrical retailer in the UK, Powerhouse, will unveil its latest results on Tuesday which are said to be much better than expected. Pre-tax profits are reportedly at 4.7 million stg against expectations of 4.4 million stg, with sales of 116.3 million stg against the predicted 115 million stg and net cash 83 percent higher than expected, at 22.9 million stg. It had been bel ieved that problems resulting from larger rivals in the sector would cause Powerhouse problems, but the retailer has announced a further six superstores will be opened in 1997, creating a further 100 jobs.
-- OTE WEIGHTED TOWARDS INSTITUTIONS

The Greek government is set to begin the second stage of privatisation of the OTE telecoms group and it is expected the pattern will be similar to that of the first offering, but with greater emphasis on international and domestic institutions. The government will sell 10.7 percent (45 million shares) of OTE's equity, offering another two percent if there is sufficient demand and will then make an other 31.6 million shares available through a 6-for-80 rights issue. The sale will be co-ordinated by the National Bank of Greece, Salomon Brothers and HSBC, who are expected to target US and UK institutional investors. --
TELEFONICA, UNISOURCE SEVER TIES

Almost a month after it defected from the Unisource telecoms alliance to join Concert, Telefonica is finally expected to reach a settlement with Unisource. Among the agreements in the settlement include the return by Telefonica of its 25 percent stake in Unisource as well as a compensatory payment made in cash of 126 million dollars to its former partners. Telefonica will be permitted to regain co ntrol of its TTD data transmission company which it handed over to Unisource as part of the equity purchase. Representatives of both sides have agreed to the proposals and it is now up to the boards of the two groups to give final approval.
